README.md.text:
# rulespec-uk

United Kingdom RuleSpec encodings in one country monorepo. Direct jurisdiction
roots include `uk/` (national) and `uk-kingston-upon-thames/` (council).
Durable ids are `<jurisdiction>:<path>#<rule>`.

## Contents

- `<jurisdiction>/{legislation,policies,regulations,statutes}/`: atomic
  `rulespec/v1` modules and companion tests.
- `<jurisdiction>/programs/`: declarative axiom-compose ProgramSpecs. Programs
  are canonical filesystem content but are not atomic RuleSpec modules.
- `.github/workflows/`: wrapper around the shared RuleSpec validation workflow.

## Conventions

Use the exact `.yaml` extension under one of the five jurisdiction-scoped roots.
Do not add repository-root content trees, `.yml` aliases, symlinks, or Python
program implementations. ProgramSpecs are declarative composition only.

Legacy applied manifests are deleted, not retained as migration inputs. This
migration snapshot intentionally contains no applied manifests; the named-release
trusted signer must regenerate `applied-rulespec/v5` attestations before release.
No workflow may accept an older schema as current attestation.

Jurisdiction-specific materials belong in this repo. Shared federal materials belong in `rulespec-us`.

uk/policies/esa_income_related_applicabl.text:
format: rulespec/v1
module:
  proof_validation:
    required: true
  source_verification:
    corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2008/794/67
  summary: |-
    Composed Family-level income-related Employment and Support Allowance
    applicable-amount and award pipeline for the 2026-27 Employment and Support
    Allowance Regulations 2008 (SI 2008/794) amounts. It exposes a
    dense-engine-friendly path from raw household facts (couple/lone-parent/
    single status, whether the eldest adult is aged 25 or over, whether the
    claimant is in the support group or the work-related activity group, the
    severe-disability and carer premium indicators, weekly assessable income,
    and any weekly housing-cost amount) into the regulation 67(1) applicable
    amount and the section 4(2)(a) income-related allowance, so an end-to-end
    comparison does not require the caller to supply the Schedule 4 amount
    selection or the means arithmetic.

    Period. The award is expressed weekly (the native period of the Schedule 4
    amounts, so every monetary value is a grounded weekly statutory rate with no
    period-conversion arithmetic).

    Scope. The applicable amount is the Schedule 4 Part A1 personal allowance
    (selected by family type and age band), plus the Part 4 income-related
    component (support component where the claimant is in the support group,
    otherwise the work-related activity component where in the work-related
    activity group), plus the Part 3 severe-disability and carer premiums where
    the indicators are set, plus a supplied weekly housing-cost amount
    (Schedule 6). The income-related allowance (section 4(2)(a) of the Welfare
    Reform Act 2007) is the applicable amount less the claimant's weekly
    assessable income, floored at zero. Deliberately outside this slice: the
    limited-capability-for-work eligibility determination (a documented input
    flag, the support-group / work-related-activity-group status); the capital
    and tariff-income rules; contributory-allowance netting; and the detailed
    Schedule 6 housing-cost mechanics (supplied as esa_ir_pilot_housing_costs_weekly).

  # Personal allowance (Schedule 4 Part A1) - weekly
  # ==========================================================================
  - name: esa_ir_pilot_personal_allowance_single_25_or_over_weekly_amount
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Employment and Support Allowance Regulations 2008, Schedule 4 Part A1, single claimant aged 25 or over or member of the work-related activity group
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2008/794/schedule/4
              excerpt: "who satisfies the conditions set out in section 4(4) of the Act or who is a member of the work-related activity group; | (a) £97.75;"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          97.75

  - name: esa_ir_pilot_personal_allowance_single_under_25_weekly_amount
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Employment and Support Allowance Regulations 2008, Schedule 4 Part A1, single claimant aged less than 25
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2008/794/schedule/4
              excerpt: "aged less than 25. | (c) £77.52."
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          77.52

  - name: esa_ir_pilot_personal_allowance_couple_weekly_amount
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Employment and Support Allowance Regulations 2008, Schedule 4 Part A1, couple both aged not less than 18
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2008/794/schedule/4
              excerpt: "where both members are aged not less than 18; | (a) £153.61;"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          153.61

  - name: esa_ir_pilot_personal_allowance_weekly
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Employment and Support Allowance Regulations 2008, Schedule 4 Part A1
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2008/794/schedule/4
              excerpt: "The weekly amounts specified in column (2) in respect of each person or couple specified in column (1)"
    versions:

          if esa_ir_pilot_is_couple:

          else:

  # ==========================================================================
  # Income-related component (Schedule 4 Part 4) - weekly
  # ==========================================================================
  - name: esa_ir_pilot_support_component_weekly_amount
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Employment and Support Allowance Regulations 2008, Schedule 4 Part 4, support component for an income-related allowance
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2008/794/schedule/4
              excerpt: "The amount of the support component for the purposes of an income-related allowance is £48.50"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          48.50

  - name: esa_ir_pilot_work_related_activity_component_weekly_amount
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Employment and Support Allowance Regulations 2008, Schedule 4 Part 4, work-related activity component for an income-related allowance
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2008/794/schedule/4
              excerpt: "The amount of the work-related activity component for the purposes of an income-related allowance is £36.55"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          36.55

  - name: esa_ir_pilot_component_weekly
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Employment and Support Allowance Regulations 2008, Schedule 4 Part 4 and regulation 67(3)
    metadata:

        atoms:

            kind: formula

  # ==========================================================================
  # Premiums (Schedule 4 Part 3) - weekly
  # ==========================================================================
  - name: esa_ir_pilot_severe_disability_premium_single_weekly_amount
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Employment and Support Allowance Regulations 2008, Schedule 4 Part 3, severe disability premium single rate
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2008/794/schedule/4
              excerpt: "where the claimant satisfies the condition in paragraph 6(2)(a); | (a) | £86.05;"

uk/policies/govuk/state-pension.yaml.text:
format: rulespec/v1
module:
  proof_validation:
    required: true
  source_verification:
    corpus_citation_path: uk/guidance/govuk/new-state-pension/what-youll-get
  summary: |-
    State pension amounts as described by GOV.UK guidance. A person who reached
    state pension age on or after 6 April 2016 gets the new state pension: the
    full weekly rate with 35 qualifying years, a proportion of it with at least
    10 qualifying years, and nothing below 10. A person who reached state
    pension age before 6 April 2016 gets the basic state pension: the full
    basic weekly rate with 30 qualifying years, and a proportion below that.
    Weekly rates are those set by the Social Security Benefits Up-rating Order
    2026.

uk/policies/universal_credit_composed_aw.text:
format: rulespec/v1
module:
  proof_validation:
    required: true
  source_verification:
    corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2012/5/8
  summary: |-
    Composed Family-level Universal Credit award pipeline for the 2026-27
    assessment-period parameters. It exposes a dense-engine-friendly path from
    raw monthly household facts (ages, couple status, number of responsible
    children, disabled-child status, limited capability for work and
    work-related activity, carer status, rent, non-dependants, childcare
    charges, earned and unearned income, capital) into the Welfare Reform Act
    2012 section 8 award so an end-to-end UKMOD bsauc_s comparison does not
    require the caller to supply the section 8 maximum-amount and deduction
    stage boundaries or the regulation 22 / 72 taper and tariff mechanics.

    It wires the section 8(2) maximum amount from the regulation 36
    standard-allowance, child, LCWRA and carer elements plus the regulation 34
    childcare-costs element and the Schedule 4 housing-costs element (net of
    regulation-13/14 non-dependant contributions); then the section 8(3)
    deductions as tariff income from capital above 6,000 (regulation 72),
    all unearned income, and 55% of earned income above the applicable
    (regulation 22) work allowance; then the regulation 80A/81 benefit-cap
    reduction; and finally the section 8(1) award, floored at zero.

    The minimum-income-floor deeming (regulation 62) is now applied on the
    pipeline: regulation 90 (the individual/couple thresholds) and the National
    Minimum Wage Regulations 2015 regulation 4 rate it points to are in the
    corpus (ingested for corpus#224), so for a claimant flagged as in gainful
    self-employment (uc_pilot_is_gainfully_self_employed) the pipeline computes
    the floor from the regulation 4 national living wage rate x the regulation
    88 expected hours (35) x 52 / 12, nets the supplied regulation 62(5)
    notional tax/NI deduction, and treats earned income below the floor as
    equal to it. A claimant who is not gainfully self-employed uses the
    supplied combined monthly earned income unchanged, so consumers that model
    employment income or floor earnings upstream keep the pre-existing
    behaviour.

    Deliberately excluded (all outside the composed household grid this slice
    models, and all separately encoded): the transitional-protection element,
    surplus-earnings and self-employment loss carry-forward mechanics, the
    Schedule 5 owner-occupier and Schedule 4 shared-ownership housing paths,
    the regulation-25 under-occupancy and bedroom-cap detail beyond the
    supplied cap rent, the start-up-period exemption and the reduced expected
    hours for carers/disability (regulation 88), and the reg 90 apprenticeship
    and regulation-3(3) single-claim couple thresholds. The two-child limit
    (former regulation 24A) is not applied: it was revoked from 6 April 2026
    for assessment periods commencing on or after that date by the Universal
    Credit (Removal of Two Child Limit) Act 2026 (c.13) s.1(3)(a), so every
    responsible child draws a child element in 2026-27.

  # ==========================================================================

  # ==========================================================================
  # Capital tariff income (regulation 72): 4.35 per 250, or part thereof,
  # above 6,000. Capital at or above the 16,000 upper limit ends entitlement

  # eligibility gate below. Input: uc_pilot_capital.
  - name: uc_pilot_capital_tariff_income
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 72(1)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/72
              excerpt: "£4.35 for each £250 in excess of £6,000 and £4.35 for any excess which is not a complete £250"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          if uc_pilot_capital > uc_pilot_capital_tariff_lower_threshold:
            uc_pilot_capital_tariff_amount_per_band * ceil((uc_pilot_capital - uc_pilot_capital_tariff_lower_threshold) / uc_pilot_capital_tariff_band_size)

            kind: condition
            source:

              excerpt: "in a case where no work allowance is specified in the table below (that is where a single claimant does not have, or neither of joint claimants has, responsibility for a child or qualifying young person or limited capability for work)"
    versions:

        formula: |-

    kind: derived

  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Regulation 62 / 90 minimum income floor for gainful self-employment
  # --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # The individual threshold that defines the floor (regulation 90(2)) is the
  # applicable National Minimum Wage / National Living Wage hourly rate for the
  # expected number of hours per week, converted to a monthly amount by
  # multiplying by 52 and dividing by 12. The pilot models a working-age
  # claimant subject to all work-related requirements (section 22), so the
  # hours figure is the regulation 88 default expected hours (35) and the rate
  # is the regulation 4 national living wage rate (21 or over). These three
  # figures are grounded in the corpus (reg 4 = 12.71, reg 88 = 35, reg 90 =
  # the 52/12 conversion) so the floor is computed here rather than supplied.
  - name: uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_national_living_wage_hourly_rate
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    unit: GBP
    source: National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015, regulation 4
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2015/621/4
              excerpt: "the national living wage rate"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          12.71

  - name: uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_expected_hours_per_week
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Count
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 88(1)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: default
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/88
              excerpt: "is 35 unless some lesser number of hours applies"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          35

  - name: uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_weeks_per_year
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Count
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 90(2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: unit
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/90
              excerpt: "multiplying by 52 and dividing by 12"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          52

  - name: uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_months_per_year
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Count
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 90(2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: unit
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/90
              excerpt: "multiplying by 52 and dividing by 12"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          12

  # Individual threshold, gross of the notional tax/NI deduction (regulation
  # 90(2): hourly rate x expected hours x 52 / 12).
  - name: uc_pilot_individual_minimum_income_floor_gross
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 90(2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/90
              excerpt: "the hourly rate applicable under regulation 4 or regulation 4A(1)(a) to (c) of the National Minimum Wage Regulations"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/90
              excerpt: "the expected number of hours per week"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/90
              excerpt: "converted to a monthly amount by multiplying by 52 and dividing by 12"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_national_living_wage_hourly_rate * uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_expected_hours_per_week * uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_weeks_per_year / uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_months_per_year

  # Applicable threshold: for a couple the floor is the sum of the individual
  # thresholds (regulation 90(3)(a)); for a single claimant it is the single
  # individual threshold. Net of the regulation 62(5) notional tax/NI
  # deduction, which the Secretary of State determines and the caller supplies
  # (uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_notional_deduction_monthly, default 0),
  # matching the regulations/uksi/2013/376/62 net-conversion input. Floored at
  # zero. Inputs: uc_pilot_is_couple,
  # uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_notional_deduction_monthly.
  - name: uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_monthly
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 62(2) and 90(3)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/90
              excerpt: "in the case of joint claimants, the sum of their individual thresholds"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/62
              excerpt: "treated as having earned income equal to that threshold"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          max(0, (if uc_pilot_is_couple: 2 * uc_pilot_individual_minimum_income_floor_gross else: uc_pilot_individual_minimum_income_floor_gross) - max(0, uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_notional_deduction_monthly))

  # Floored earned income for the deduction. For a claimant in gainful
  # self-employment (regulation 62), earned income below the minimum income
  # floor is treated as equal to the floor; the floor is now computed here
  # from regulation 90 rather than supplied. For a claimant who is not
  # gainfully self-employed, the pipeline uses the supplied combined monthly
  # earned income unchanged, so consumers that already floor earnings upstream
  # or model employment income keep the pre-existing behaviour. Inputs:
  # uc_pilot_is_gainfully_self_employed, uc_pilot_earned_income_monthly.
  - name: uc_pilot_floored_earned_income_monthly
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 62(2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/62
              excerpt: "the claimant is to be treated as having earned income equal to that threshold"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          if uc_pilot_is_gainfully_self_employed and max(0, uc_pilot_earned_income_monthly) < uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_monthly: uc_pilot_minimum_income_floor_monthly else: max(0, uc_pilot_earned_income_monthly)

  # Earned income above the work allowance (regulation 22(1)(b)), tapered
  # below. Consumes the floored earned income so the regulation 62 minimum
  # income floor is applied for gainful self-employment; for every other case
  # the floored amount equals the supplied combined monthly earned income.
  - name: uc_pilot_earned_income_above_work_allowance
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 22(1)(b)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/22
              excerpt: "55% of the amount by which that earned income exceeds the work allowance"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          max(0, uc_pilot_floored_earned_income_monthly - uc_pilot_applicable_work_allowance)

  - name: uc_pilot_earned_income_deduction
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 22(1)(b)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/22
              excerpt: "55% of that earned income"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          uc_pilot_earned_income_taper_rate * uc_pilot_earned_income_above_work_allowance

  # Section 8(3) total deduction: all unearned income (including capital
  # tariff income, which regulation 66 treats as unearned income) plus the
  # tapered earned income. Input: uc_pilot_unearned_income_monthly.
  - name: uc_pilot_total_deduction
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Welfare Reform Act 2012 s.8(3); Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 22(1)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/22
              excerpt: "The amounts to be deducted from the maximum amount in accordance with section 8(3) of the Act to determine the amount of an award of universal credit are—"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          max(0, uc_pilot_unearned_income_monthly) + uc_pilot_capital_tariff_income + uc_pilot_earned_income_deduction

  # ==========================================================================
  # Section 8(1) award before the benefit cap
  # ==========================================================================
  # Capital eligibility gate (regulation 18): capital at or above the upper
  # limit ends entitlement. Input: uc_pilot_capital.
  - name: uc_pilot_capital_over_upper_limit
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Judgment
    period: Month
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 18
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: condition
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/18
              excerpt: "the prescribed amount for a single claimant is £16,000"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          uc_pilot_capital >= uc_pilot_capital_upper_limit

  - name: uc_pilot_award_before_cap
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Welfare Reform Act 2012 s.8(1)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2012/5/8
              excerpt: "The amount of an award of universal credit is to be the balance of—"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          if uc_pilot_capital_over_upper_limit: 0 else: max(0, uc_pilot_maximum_amount - uc_pilot_total_deduction)

  # ==========================================================================
  # Regulation 80A/81 benefit cap
  # ==========================================================================
  # Applicable annual limit by case (regulation 80A(2)): single claimants with
  # no responsible child use the lower single limits; couples and claimants
  # with a responsible child use the higher limits; each is uprated by
  # Greater-London residence. Inputs: uc_pilot_is_couple,
  # uc_pilot_number_of_responsible_children, uc_pilot_resident_in_greater_london.
  - name: uc_pilot_benefit_cap_annual_limit
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 80A(2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/80A
              excerpt: "The applicable annual limit is—"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          if uc_pilot_is_couple or uc_pilot_number_of_responsible_children >= 1:
            if uc_pilot_resident_in_greater_london: uc_pilot_benefit_cap_annual_limit_couple_or_single_with_child_in_london else: uc_pilot_benefit_cap_annual_limit_couple_or_single_with_child_outside_london
          else:
            if uc_pilot_resident_in_greater_london: uc_pilot_benefit_cap_annual_limit_single_no_child_in_london else: uc_pilot_benefit_cap_annual_limit_single_no_child_outside_london

  - name: uc_pilot_benefit_cap_monthly_limit
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 80A(1)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/80A
              excerpt: "The relevant amount is determined by dividing the applicable annual limit by 12."
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          uc_pilot_benefit_cap_annual_limit / uc_pilot_benefit_cap_annual_divisor

  # Benefit cap reduction (regulation 81 and 82). The cap does not apply where
  # the claimant is within the earnings exception; where it applies, the award
  # is reduced by the excess of total welfare benefits over the relevant
  # amount, less any childcare costs element (regulation 81(1)(b)/(2)). This
  # pipeline compares the pre-cap award (its own welfare-benefit total for the
  # single-benefit UC household) against the monthly cap. Inputs:
  # uc_pilot_exempt_from_benefit_cap.
  - name: uc_pilot_benefit_cap_excess
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 81(3)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/81
              excerpt: "The excess is the total amount of welfare benefits that the single person or the couple are entitled to in the reference period, minus the relevant amount determined under regulation 80A"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          max(0, uc_pilot_award_before_cap - uc_pilot_benefit_cap_monthly_limit)

  - name: uc_pilot_benefit_cap_reduction
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 81(1) and 81(2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/81
              excerpt: "the amount of the award for that period is to be reduced by—"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/81
              excerpt: "any amount included in the award for the childcare costs element"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          if uc_pilot_exempt_from_benefit_cap:
            0
          else:
            if uc_pilot_childcare_element > uc_pilot_benefit_cap_excess: 0 else: uc_pilot_benefit_cap_excess - uc_pilot_childcare_element

  # ==========================================================================
  # Final award
  # ==========================================================================
  - name: uc_pilot_award_amount
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: Welfare Reform Act 2012 s.8(1); Universal Credit Regulations 2013, regulation 81
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2012/5/8
              excerpt: "The amount of an award of universal credit"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2026-04-01'
        formula: |-
          max(0, uc_pilot_award_before_cap - uc_pilot_benefit_cap_reduction)

format: rulespec/v1
module:
  proof_validation:
    required: true
  source_verification:
    corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
  summary: |-
    Income Support capital between the applicable lower threshold and GBP 16,000 is treated as weekly income of GBP 1 for each complete or incomplete GBP 250 above that threshold. The ordinary lower threshold is GBP 6,000, with a GBP 10,000 lower threshold for claimants to whom paragraph (1B) applies.

            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "exceeds £6,000"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '1988-04-11'
        formula: |-
          6000

  - name: prescribed_accommodation_capital_tariff_income_lower_threshold
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Support (General) Regulations 1987, regulation 53(1A)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:

            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "exceeds £10,000"

        formula: |-
          10000

  - name: capital_tariff_income_upper_limit
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Support (General) Regulations 1987, regulation 53(1), (1A)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "but not exceeding £16,000"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '1988-04-11'
        formula: |-
          16000

  - name: capital_tariff_income_band_size
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Support (General) Regulations 1987, regulation 53(1), (2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "for each complete £250"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '1988-04-11'
        formula: |-
          250

  - name: capital_tariff_income_weekly_amount_per_band
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Support (General) Regulations 1987, regulation 53(1), (2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "weekly income of £1"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '1988-04-11'
        formula: |-
          1

  - name: applicable_capital_tariff_income_lower_threshold
    kind: derived
    entity: Person
    dtype: Money
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Support (General) Regulations 1987, regulation 53(1)-(1B)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "Except where the circumstances prescribed in paragraph"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "circumstances prescribed in paragraph (1B) apply"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '1988-04-11'
        formula: |-
          if claimant_in_prescribed_accommodation_under_regulation_53_1B: prescribed_accommodation_capital_tariff_income_lower_threshold else: ordinary_capital_tariff_income_lower_threshold

  - name: capital_treated_as_yielding_weekly_income
    kind: derived
    entity: Person
    dtype: Judgment
    period: Week
    source: Income Support (General) Regulations 1987, regulation 53(1), (1A)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "it shall be treated as equivalent to a weekly income"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: condition
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "but not exceeding £16,000"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '1988-04-11'
        formula: |-
          claimant_capital > applicable_capital_tariff_income_lower_threshold
          and claimant_capital <= capital_tariff_income_upper_limit

  - name: capital_tariff_weekly_income
    kind: derived
    entity: Person
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Support (General) Regulations 1987, regulation 53(1), (1A), (2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "£1 for each complete £250"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/1987/1967/53
              excerpt: "not a complete £250"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '1988-04-11'
        formula: |-
          if capital_treated_as_yielding_weekly_income: capital_tariff_income_weekly_amount_per_band * ceil((claimant_capital - applicable_capital_tariff_income_lower_threshold) / capital_tariff_income_band_size) else: 0

uk/regulations/uksi/2013/376/80A.yaml.text:
format: rulespec/v1
module:
  proof_validation:
    required: true
  source_verification:
    corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/80A
  summary: |-
    The relevant amount is determined by dividing the applicable annual limit by 12. The applicable annual limit is £16,967, £25,323, £14,753 or £22,020 according to claimant status, Greater London residence, and responsibility for a child or qualifying young person. A claimant is resident in Greater London according to the stated housing-costs, housing-benefit, home, or allocated Jobcentre Plus office tests.
rules:
  - name: benefit_cap_relevant_amount_annual_divisor
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Count
    source: regulation 80A(1)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/80A
              excerpt: "dividing the applicable annual limit by 12"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2013-04-29'
        formula: |-
          12

  - name: benefit_cap_applicable_annual_limit_by_case
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    unit: GBP
    indexed_by: benefit_cap_applicable_annual_limit_case
    source: regulation 80A(2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].values
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/80A
              excerpt: "The applicable annual limit is—\n£16,967 for a single claimant resident in Greater London who is not responsible for a child or qualifying young person;\n£25,323 for—\njoint claimants where either joint claimant is resident in Greater London;\na single claimant resident in Greater London who is responsible for a child or qualifying young person;\n£14,753 for a single claimant not resident in Greater London who is not responsible for a child or qualifying young person;\n£22,020 for—\njoint claimants not resident in Greater London;\na single claimant not resident in Greater London who is responsible for a child or qualifying young person."
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2013-04-29'
        values:
          0: 16967
          1: 25323
          2: 14753
          3: 22020

  - name: claimant_or_either_joint_claimant_resident_in_greater_london
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Judgment
    period: Month
    source: regulation 80A(3)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: definition
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/80A
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2013-04-29'
        formula: |-
          (award_contains_housing_costs_element
          and (
            accommodation_in_respect_of_which_claimant_meets_occupation_condition_is_in_greater_london
            or claimant_receives_housing_benefit_for_dwelling_in_greater_london
          ))
          or (
            not award_contains_housing_costs_element
            and (
              accommodation_normally_occupied_as_home_is_in_greater_london
              or (
                not claimant_has_accommodation_normally_occupied_as_home
                and jobcentre_plus_office_allocated_to_claim_is_in_greater_london
              )
            )
          )

  - name: benefit_cap_applicable_annual_limit_case
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Integer
    period: Month
    source: regulation 80A(2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: condition
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/80A
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2013-04-29'
        formula: |-
          if claim_is_for_joint_claimants: (if claimant_or_either_joint_claimant_resident_in_greater_london: 1 else: 3) else: (if claimant_or_either_joint_claimant_resident_in_greater_london: (if responsible_for_child_or_qualifying_young_person: 1 else: 0) else: (if responsible_for_child_or_qualifying_young_person: 3 else: 2))

  - name: benefit_cap_applicable_annual_limit_for_claim
    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: regulation 80A(2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:

            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/80A
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2013-04-29'
        formula: |-
          benefit_cap_applicable_annual_limit_by_case[benefit_cap_applicable_annual_limit_case]

    kind: derived
    entity: Family
    dtype: Money
    period: Month
    unit: GBP
    source: regulation 80A(1)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/regulation/uksi/2013/376/80A
              excerpt: "The relevant amount is determined by dividing the applicable annual limit by 12."
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2013-04-29'
        formula: |-

format: rulespec/v1
module:
  proof_validation:
    required: true
  source_verification:
    corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/anaw/2017/1/24
  summary: |-
    The Welsh Ministers must by regulations specify the tax bands and percentage tax rates for residential, higher rates residential, and non-residential property transactions. Regulations for residential and non-residential transactions must include a 0% zero rate band and two or more bands above it; higher rates residential regulations must specify three or more tax bands. A chargeable transaction is residential if its main subject-matter consists entirely of residential property interests, higher rates residential if Schedule 5 applies, and non-residential if its main subject-matter consists of or includes non-residential land interests. The specified bands and rates do not apply to chargeable consideration that is rent.
rules:
  - name: zero_rate_band_tax_rate
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Rate
    source: subsection (3)(a)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: parameter
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/anaw/2017/1/24
              excerpt: "a tax band for which the applicable tax rate is 0% (““the zero rate band””),"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '0001-01-01'
        formula: |-
          0

  - name: minimum_bands_above_zero_rate_band
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Count
    source: subsection (3)(b)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: parameter
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/anaw/2017/1/24
              excerpt: 'two or more tax bands above the zero rate band'
    versions:
      - effective_from: '0001-01-01'
        formula: |-
          2

  - name: minimum_higher_rates_residential_tax_bands
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Count
    source: subsection (4)(a)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: parameter
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/anaw/2017/1/24
              excerpt: 'three or more tax bands'
    versions:
      - effective_from: '0001-01-01'
        formula: |-
          3

  - name: residential_property_transaction
    kind: derived
    entity: ChargeableTransaction
    dtype: Judgment
    period: Day
    source: subsection (6)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula

            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/anaw/2017/1/24
    versions:
      - effective_from: '0001-01-01'
        formula: |-
          transaction_is_chargeable
          and (
            main_subject_matter_consists_entirely_of_residential_property_interest
            or (
              transaction_is_one_of_linked_transactions
              and each_linked_transaction_main_subject_matter_consists_entirely_of_residential_property_interest
            )
          )

  - name: higher_rates_residential_property_transaction
    kind: derived
    entity: ChargeableTransaction

    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:

            kind: definition
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/anaw/2017/1/24
    versions:
      - effective_from: '0001-01-01'
        formula: |-
          transaction_is_chargeable
          and schedule_5_applies_to_transaction

    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:

    versions:

          transaction_is_chargeable
          and (
            main_subject_matter_consists_of_or_includes_non_residential_land_interest
            or (
              transaction_is_one_of_linked_transactions
              and any_linked_transaction_main_subject_matter_consists_of_or_includes_non_residential_land_interest
            )
          )

uk/statutes/ukpga/1992/4/13.yaml.text:
format: rulespec/v1
module:
  proof_validation:
    required: true
  source_verification:
    corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/1992/4/13
  summary: |-
    Class 3 National Insurance contributions are voluntary flat-rate
    contributions. Section 13 of the Social Security Contributions and Benefits
    Act 1992 provides for earners and others over the age of 16 to be entitled,
    if they so wish and subject to prescribed conditions, to pay Class 3
    contributions; the amount of a Class 3 contribution is a flat weekly
    figure. The s.13(1) base text on legislation.gov.uk reads £17.75, the
    2025-26 rate; the annual administrative re-rating is not consolidated into
    the base text, and the GOV.UK "Rates and allowances: National Insurance
    contributions" guidance carries the 2026-27 weekly rate of £18.40 from
    6 April 2026. Payment is allowed only with a view to enabling the
    contributor to satisfy conditions of entitlement to benefit by acquiring
    the requisite earnings factor. Because Class 3 is elective, the payment is only made when
    the contributor chooses to pay: the contribution amount is the flat rate for
    each week for which the contributor elects to pay, and zero otherwise. The
    election, the over-16 condition, the satisfaction of the prescribed
    conditions, and the benefit-purpose condition are supplied as case inputs.
rules:
  - name: class_3_weekly_contribution_amount
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    period: Week
    unit: GBP
    source: Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992 s.13(1), as re-rated for 2026-27 per GOV.UK rates and allowances guidance
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/1992/4/13
              excerpt: "shall be £17.75"
          - path: versions[1].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/guidance/govuk/national-insurance-rates/rates-and-allowances/block-11
              excerpt: "Class 3 rate £18.40"
          - path: versions[1].effective_from
            kind: effective_period
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/guidance/govuk/national-insurance-rates/rates-and-allowances/block-11
              excerpt: "£ per week 2026 to 2027"
          - path: versions[1].effective_from
            kind: effective_period
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/guidance/govuk/national-insurance-rates/rates-and-allowances/block-13
              excerpt: "new National Insurance rates and thresholds from 6 April 2026"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2025-04-06'
        formula: |-
          17.75
      - effective_from: '2026-04-06'
        formula: |-
          18.40

  - name: entitled_to_pay_class_3_contribution
    kind: derived
    entity: Person
    dtype: Judgment
    period: Week
    source: Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992 s.13(1), (2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: condition

uk/statutes/ukpga/2007/3/35.yaml.text:
format: rulespec/v1
module:
  proof_validation:
    required: true
  source_verification:
    corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/35
  summary: |-
    An individual who makes a claim is entitled to a personal allowance of £12,570 for a tax year if the individual meets the requirements of section 56; where adjusted net income exceeds £100,000, the allowance is reduced by one-half of the excess and any remaining allowance is rounded up to the nearest £1.

          12570

  - name: adjusted_net_income_reduction_threshold

    versions:

        formula: |-

        atoms:

    metadata:

        atoms:

          1

              excerpt: "allowance under subsection (1) is reduced by one-half of the excess"

            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/35
              excerpt: "rounded up to the nearest amount which is a multiple of £1"

            kind: import
            import:
              target: uk:statutes/ukpga/2007/3/35#personal_allowance_base_amount
              output: personal_allowance_base_amount
              hash: sha256:local

uk/statutes/ukpga/2007/3/55B.yaml.text:
format: rulespec/v1
module:
  proof_validation:
    required: true
  source_verification:
    corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
  summary: |-
    Marriage Allowance. Section 55B of the Income Tax Act 2007 entitles an
    individual to a tax reduction of the appropriate percentage of the
    transferable amount where the conditions in subsection (2) are met: the
    individual is the gaining party under a section 55C election in force for
    the year, is not liable to tax at a rate other than the basic rate (or the
    equivalent starter/basic/intermediate rates for a Scottish or Welsh
    taxpayer), meets the residence requirement, and neither party claims the
    married couple's allowance. The transferable amount for 2015-16 is £1,060
    and, for 2016-17 and subsequent tax years, is 10% of the personal allowance
    specified in section 35(1) for the year, rounded up to the nearest £10. The
    transferring spouse or civil partner can transfer no more personal allowance
    than they leave unused, so the amount actually transferred is the lesser of
    the statutory 10%-of-personal-allowance figure and the transferor's unused
    personal allowance. The personal allowance for the year and the transferor's
    unused personal allowance are supplied as case inputs; whether each
    subsection (2) condition is met is supplied as case inputs.
rules:
  - name: appropriate_percentage_of_personal_allowance
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Rate
    source: Income Tax Act 2007 s.55B(4)(b)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: parameter
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
              excerpt: "is 10% of the amount of personal allowance specified in section 35(1)"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2016-04-06'
        formula: |-
          0.10

  - name: transferable_amount_rounding_multiple
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Tax Act 2007 s.55B(5)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
              excerpt: "rounded up to the nearest amount which is a multiple of £10"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2016-04-06'
        formula: |-
          10

  - name: transferable_amount_2015_16
    kind: parameter
    dtype: Money
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Tax Act 2007 s.55B(4)(a)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: amount
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
              excerpt: "for the tax year 2015-16, is £1,060"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2015-04-06'
        formula: |-
          1060

  - name: individual_entitled_to_marriage_allowance_tax_reduction
    kind: derived
    entity: Person
    dtype: Judgment
    period: Year
    source: Income Tax Act 2007 s.55B(1), (2)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: condition
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
              excerpt: "the individual is the gaining party"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: condition
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
              excerpt: "not, for the tax year, liable to tax at a rate other than the basic rate"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: condition
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
              excerpt: "the individual meets the requirements of section 56 (residence)"
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2015-04-06'
        formula: |-
          individual_is_the_gaining_party_under_a_section_55c_election
          and individual_not_liable_above_basic_rate
          and individual_meets_section_56_residence_requirement
          and neither_party_claims_married_couples_allowance

  - name: statutory_transferable_amount
    kind: derived
    entity: Person
    dtype: Money
    period: Year
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Tax Act 2007 s.55B(4)(b), (5)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
              excerpt: "is 10% of the amount of personal allowance specified in section 35(1)"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
              excerpt: "rounded up to the nearest amount which is a multiple of £10"
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: import
            import:
              target: uk:statutes/ukpga/2007/3/55B#appropriate_percentage_of_personal_allowance
              output: appropriate_percentage_of_personal_allowance
              hash: sha256:local
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: import
            import:
              target: uk:statutes/ukpga/2007/3/55B#transferable_amount_rounding_multiple
              output: transferable_amount_rounding_multiple
              hash: sha256:local
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2016-04-06'
        formula: |-
          ceil((appropriate_percentage_of_personal_allowance * personal_allowance_specified_in_section_35_1) / transferable_amount_rounding_multiple) * transferable_amount_rounding_multiple

  - name: transferable_amount
    kind: derived
    entity: Person
    dtype: Money
    period: Year
    unit: GBP
    source: Income Tax Act 2007 s.55B(1), (4)(b), (5), (6)
    metadata:
      proof:
        atoms:
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: formula
            source:
              corpus_citation_path: uk/statute/ukpga/2007/3/55B
              excerpt: "6) If an individual is entitled to a tax reduction under subsection (1) by reference to an election under section 55C , the personal allowance to which the relinquishing spouse or civil partner is entitled under section 35  ... is reduced for the tax year by the transferable amount."
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: import
            import:
              target: uk:statutes/ukpga/2007/3/55B#statutory_transferable_amount
              output: statutory_transferable_amount
              hash: sha256:local
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: import
            import:
              target: uk:statutes/ukpga/2007/3/55B#transferable_amount_rounding_multiple
              output: transferable_amount_rounding_multiple
              hash: sha256:local
          - path: versions[0].formula
            kind: import
            import:
              target: uk:statutes/ukpga/2007/3/55B#individual_entitled_to_marriage_allowance_tax_reduction
              output: individual_entitled_to_marriage_allowance_tax_reduction
              hash: sha256:local
    versions:
      - effective_from: '2016-04-06'
        formula: |-
          if individual_entitled_to_marriage_allowance_tax_reduction: ceil(max(0, min(relinquishing_partner_unused_personal_allowance, statutory_transferable_amount)) / transferable_amount_rounding_multiple) * transferable_amount_rounding_multiple else: 0

# The timetable is keyed from the Pensions Act 1995 and reflects its current
# text, last amended by the Pensions Act 2014 (section 26, in force 14 July
# 2014). Earlier versions are not encoded separately: every amendment moved
# only people who had not yet reached pensionable age, so the timetable gives
# the right status for any past date.
#
# Dates of birth and days are written as YYYYMMDD numbers. Each bracket runs
# from its threshold (inclusive) to the next threshold.

# An age of N years and M months is attained on the same day of the month, or
# on the month's last day where that day does not exist. That gives the three
# days rule (7A) sets for table 3: 30 November 2026 for a birthday on 31 July

    amount:

# Standard library imports
import copy
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List

# PolicyEngine core imports
from policyengine_core.parameters.operations.propagate_parameter_metadata import (
    propagate_parameter_metadata,
)
from policyengine_core.parameters.operations.uprate_parameters import (
    uprate_parameters,
)
from policyengine_core.taxbenefitsystems import TaxBenefitSystem
from policyengine_core.variables import Variable

# PolicyEngine UK imports
from policyengine_uk.entities import BenUnit, Household, Person
from policyengine_uk.parameters.gov.contrib.create_private_pension_uprating import (
    add_private_pension_uprating_factor,
)
from policyengine_uk.parameters.gov.dwp.state_pension.triple_lock.create_triple_lock import (
    add_triple_lock,
)
from policyengine_uk.parameters.gov.economic_assumptions.create_economic_assumption_indices import (
    create_economic_assumption_indices,
)
from policyengine_uk.parameters.gov.economic_assumptions.create_statutory_uprating_inputs import (
    add_statutory_uprating_inputs,
)
from policyengine_uk.parameters.gov.economic_assumptions.lag_average_earnings import (
    add_lagged_earnings,
)
from policyengine_uk.parameters.gov.economic_assumptions.lag_cpi import (
    add_lagged_cpi,
)
from policyengine_uk.parameters.gov.simulation.labour_supply_responses.aliases import (
    add_lsr_deprecation_aliases,
)
from policyengine_uk.utils.parameters import (
    add_removed_parameter_aliases,
    backdate_parameters,
    convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters,
)

# Module constants
COUNTRY_DIR = Path(__file__).parent
DEFAULT_DATASET_ENV_VAR = "POLICYENGINE_UK_DEFAULT_DATASET"

# Cache for fully-processed parameter tree, so convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters
# (22,538 param.update() calls) only runs once per process.
_processed_parameters_cache = None


class CountryTaxBenefitSystem(TaxBenefitSystem):
    """UK-specific tax and benefit system implementation.

    This class defines the UK tax-benefit system with all relevant
    variables, parameters, and entities (Person, BenUnit, Household).
    """

    basic_inputs: List[str] = [
        "brma",
        "local_authority",
        "region",
        "employment_income",
        "age",
    ]
    modelled_policies = COUNTRY_DIR / "programs.yaml"
    auto_carry_over_input_variables: bool = True

    variables: Dict[str, Variable]

    def reset_parameter_caches(self):
        """Reset all caches in the tax-benefit system."""
        self._parameters_at_instant_cache = {}
        for parameter in self.parameters.get_descendants():
            parameter._at_instant_cache = {}
        self.parameters._at_instant_cache = {}

    def reset_parameters(self) -> None:
        """Reset parameters by reloading from the parameters directory."""
        self._parameters_at_instant_cache = {}
        self.load_parameters(self.parameters_dir)
        self.parameters = add_removed_parameter_aliases(self.parameters)

    def process_parameters(self) -> None:
        """Process and transform parameters with UK-specific adjustments.

        Applies various parameter transformations including:
        - Private pension uprating factors
        - Lagged earnings and CPI indices
        - Statutory uprating inputs (September CPI, May-July earnings)
        - Triple lock calculations for state pensions
        - Economic assumption indices
        - Parameter uprating and backdating
        - Conversion to fiscal year parameters
        """
        self._parameters_at_instant_cache = {}
        # Add various UK-specific parameter adjustments
        self.parameters = add_private_pension_uprating_factor(self.parameters)
        self.parameters = add_lagged_earnings(self.parameters)
        self.parameters = add_lagged_cpi(self.parameters)
        self.parameters = add_statutory_uprating_inputs(self.parameters)
        self.parameters = add_triple_lock(self.parameters)
        self.parameters = create_economic_assumption_indices(self.parameters)
        self.parameters = add_lsr_deprecation_aliases(self.parameters)

        # Create baseline parameters for reform comparisons
        self.parameters.add_child("baseline", self.parameters.clone())

        # Apply general parameter operations
        self.parameters = propagate_parameter_metadata(self.parameters)
        self.parameters = uprate_parameters(self.parameters)
        self.parameters = backdate_parameters(self.parameters, "2015-01-01")
        self.parameters.gov = convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters(self.parameters.gov)
        self.reset_parameter_caches()

    def __init__(self):
        """Initialize the UK tax-benefit system with entities and parameters."""
        self._parameters_at_instant_cache: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        self.variables = {}

        # Create copies of entity classes to avoid modifying originals
        person, benunit, household = (
            copy.copy(Person),
            copy.copy(BenUnit),
            copy.copy(Household),
        )

        # Set up entities
        self.entities = [person, benunit, household]
        self.person_entity = person
        self.group_entities = [benunit, household]
        self.group_entity_keys = [entity.key for entity in self.group_entities]

        # Link entities to this tax-benefit system
        for entity in self.entities:
            entity.set_tax_benefit_system(self)

        self.variable_module_metadata = {}

        # Load all variables from the variables directory
        self.add_variables_from_directory(COUNTRY_DIR / "variables")

        # Set up and process parameters
        self.parameters_dir = COUNTRY_DIR / "parameters"
        global _processed_parameters_cache
        if _processed_parameters_cache is not None:
            # Fast path: clone pre-processed parameters rather than re-running
            # the full pipeline (saves ~0.5s from convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters).
            # apply_parameter_changes() calls reset_parameters() + process_parameters()
            # directly, so reforms still get the full pipeline.
            self._parameters_at_instant_cache = {}
            self.parameters = _processed_parameters_cache.clone()
        else:
            self.reset_parameters()
            self.process_parameters()
            _processed_parameters_cache = self.parameters.clone()


# Create system instance for module-level access
system = CountryTaxBenefitSystem()
parameters = system.parameters
variables = system.variables

import datetime

from policyengine_core.model_api import *
from policyengine_core import periods


def str_to_instant(s):
    return periods.Instant(tuple(map(lambda s: int(s), s.split("-"))))


def backdate_parameters(root: str = None, first_instant: str = "2021-01-01") -> Reform:
    first_instant = str_to_instant(first_instant)
    node = root
    for param in node.get_descendants():
        if isinstance(param, Parameter):
            earliest = param.values_list[-1]
            earliest_value = earliest.value
            earliest_instant = str_to_instant(earliest.instant_str)
            if first_instant < earliest_instant:
                num_days = (earliest_instant.date - first_instant.date).days
                param.update(
                    period=periods.Period(("day", first_instant, num_days)),
                    value=earliest_value,
                )
    return root


def fiscal_year_average(param, year: int):
    """Day-weighted average of a parameter across a UK fiscal year.

    Returns None where any value in the year is missing or non-numeric, so
    the caller can fall back to sampling a single date.
    """
    start = datetime.date(year, 4, 6)
    end = datetime.date(year + 1, 4, 6)

    changes = []
    for value_at_instant in param.values_list:
        try:
            instant = datetime.date.fromisoformat(value_at_instant.instant_str)
        except ValueError:
            return None
        if start < instant < end:
            changes.append(instant)

    boundaries = [start, *sorted(changes), end]
    total = 0.0
    for segment_start, segment_end in zip(boundaries, boundaries[1:]):
        value = param(segment_start.isoformat())
        if not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or isinstance(value, bool):
            return None
        total += value * (segment_end - segment_start).days

    return total / (end - start).days


def uk_fiscal_year_period(time_period):
    """Translate a bare year into the UK fiscal year it names.

    A UK parameter change for "2025" means the fiscal year starting 6 April
    2025. Writing it as the calendar year leaves January to April of 2026
    on prior law, which fiscal-year conversion then blends into the value —
    an annual override of 0.5 came out as 0.42. Non-year periods pass
    through untouched.
    """
    year = None
    if isinstance(time_period, int):
        year = time_period
    elif isinstance(time_period, str) and time_period.strip().isdigit():
        year = int(time_period.strip())
    if year is None or not 1900 < year < 2200:
        return time_period
    start = periods.Instant((year, 4, 6))
    days = (datetime.date(year + 1, 4, 6) - datetime.date(year, 4, 6)).days
    return periods.Period(("day", start, days))


def convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters(parameters):
    """
    Convert parameters to use UK fiscal year values.

    The UK fiscal year runs April 6 to April 5. When querying a parameter
    for a year (e.g., param("2026")), we want the value at April 30 of
    that year (which represents the fiscal year starting April 6).

    This function samples each parameter at April 30 of each year and
    sets that as the value for the entire year period.

    Sampling a single date drops any change taking effect later in the fiscal
    year. Parameters carrying `fiscal_year_blend: true` in their metadata are
    day-weighted across the year instead, which is the right annualisation for
    a rate or threshold that applies to a flow spread over the year. Leave the
    flag off where the value at a point in time is what applies, as for a tax
    charged on a transaction at the rate in force on its date.

    Parameters with ``preserve_calendar_dates: true`` retain statutory dates.
    Their formulas must explicitly annualise the underlying transactions.

    Values are computed for every year before any are written, so that
    rewriting one year cannot affect the reading of another.
    """
    # Cover years from 2015 through 2040 for long-term projections
    YEARS = list(range(2015, 2041))
    for param in parameters.get_descendants():
        if isinstance(param, Parameter):
            if (param.metadata or {}).get("preserve_calendar_dates", False):
                continue
            blend = (param.metadata or {}).get("fiscal_year_blend", False)
            values = {}
            for year in YEARS:
                value = fiscal_year_average(param, year) if blend else None
                if value is None:
                    value = param(f"{year}-04-30")
                values[year] = value
            for year, value in values.items():
                param.update(
                    period=f"{year}",
                    value=value,
                )
    return parameters


_STATE_PENSION_AGE_REPLACEMENT = (
    "State Pension age now follows the statutory timetable by date of birth "
    "(Pensions Act 1995 Sch 4 para 1). Change the rows of "
    "gov.dwp.state_pension.age.age_by_birth_date (the age, in months) or "
    "gov.dwp.state_pension.age.day_by_birth_date (the day) for the births you "
    "want to change, for example gov.dwp.state_pension.age.age_by_birth_date[14]"
    ".amount for people born from 6 March 1961 until the next bracket, or "
    "gov.dwp.state_pension.age.male.age for men born before 6 December 1953. "
    "Read a person's State Pension age from the state_pension_age or is_SP_age "
    "variables."
)

# Parameters removed from the tree, with what replaces them, so a reform or
# saved policy that still names one fails with directions instead of a bare
# lookup error.
REMOVED_PARAMETERS = {
    "gov.dwp.state_pension.age.male": _STATE_PENSION_AGE_REPLACEMENT,
    "gov.dwp.state_pension.age.female": _STATE_PENSION_AGE_REPLACEMENT,
}


def check_parameter_not_removed(path: str) -> None:
    """Raise a ValueError naming the replacement if path was removed."""
    if path in REMOVED_PARAMETERS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"The parameter {path} has been removed. {REMOVED_PARAMETERS[path]}"
        )


class RemovedParameterNode(ParameterNode):
    """Keep a removed path discoverable without accepting scalar reforms.

    Male State Pension age still has valid children, so the compatibility
    node must support normal tree traversal and cloning. API reform code
    reads values_list before updating; both operations give migration help.
    """

    @property
    def values_list(self):
        check_parameter_not_removed(self.name)

    def update(self, *args, **kwargs):
        check_parameter_not_removed(self.name)


class RemovedParameterRoot(ParameterNode):
    """Reject explicit lookups of removed scalars, including empty policies."""

    def get_child(self, path: str):
        check_parameter_not_removed(path)
        return super().get_child(path)


def add_removed_parameter_aliases(parameters: ParameterNode) -> ParameterNode:
    if not isinstance(parameters, RemovedParameterRoot):
        root = RemovedParameterRoot(parameters.name, data={})
        root.__dict__ = parameters.__dict__.copy()
        for child in root.children.values():
            child.parent = root
        parameters = root
    age = parameters.gov.dwp.state_pension.age
    for path, replacement in REMOVED_PARAMETERS.items():
        name = path.rsplit(".", 1)[1]
        previous = age.children.get(name)
        if isinstance(previous, RemovedParameterNode):
            continue
        alias = RemovedParameterNode(path, data={})
        if previous is not None:
            alias.metadata.update(previous.metadata)
            for child_name, child in previous.children.items():
                alias.add_child(child_name, child)
        alias.description = f"The parameter {path} has been removed. {replacement}"
        alias.metadata.update(
            label=f"removed {name} State Pension age parameter",
            removed=True,
            economy=False,
            household=False,
        )
        age.children[name] = alias
        setattr(age, name, alias)
        alias.parent = age
    return parameters

utils/state_pension_age.py.text:
"""Pensionable age by date of birth, and ages that follow its timetable.

Pensions Act 1995 Schedule 4 paragraph 1 sets pensionable age (State Pension
age) by date of birth. Rule (1) gives men born before 6 December 1953 the age
of 65; the other rules set an age or a day for everyone else, including every
woman. The qualifying age for State Pension Credit (State Pension Credit Act
2002 s.1(6)) is a woman's pensionable age, and for a man the pensionable age of
a woman born on the same day: the same timetable without rule (1).

Dates are measured in months on the grid in policyengine_uk.utils.dates, whose
months start on the 6th, so the middle of the fiscal year (6 October) is a
whole month.
"""

import numpy as np

from policyengine_uk.utils.dates import (
    add_months_to_yyyymmdd,
    grid_month,
    yyyymmdd_to_grid_months,
)


def age_attaining_pensionable_age(
    timetable, birth, birth_date, male_rule
) -> np.ndarray:
    """The age, in years, at which pensionable age is attained.

    ``timetable`` is the gov.dwp.state_pension.age parameter node. Where
    ``male_rule`` is true, rule (1) applies (the male age); elsewhere the
    timetable in rules (2) to (10) sets an age or a day, and the later of the
    two is when pensionable age is attained.
    """
    age_rule = np.where(
        male_rule, timetable.male.age, timetable.age_by_birth_date.calc(birth_date)
    )
    day_rule = np.where(male_rule, 0, timetable.day_by_birth_date.calc(birth_date))
    day_rule_month = np.where(
        day_rule > 0,
        yyyymmdd_to_grid_months(np.maximum(day_rule, 10101)),
        -np.inf,
    )
    # An age of N years and M months is attained at the commencement of the
    # anniversary (Family Law Reform Act 1969 s.9(1)): the same day of the
    # month, or the month's last day where that day does not exist, which
    # also gives the three days in rule (7A).
    anniversary = yyyymmdd_to_grid_months(add_months_to_yyyymmdd(birth_date, age_rule))
    attained = np.maximum(anniversary, day_rule_month)
    return (attained - birth) / 12


def months_since_attaining(birth, year: int, attained_age) -> np.ndarray:
    """Months between attaining ``attained_age`` and 6 October of the fiscal
    year starting in ``year``; negative if the person attains it later.

    ``birth`` is the instant of birth in grid months, the same instant the
    attained age was measured from (policyengine_uk.utils.dates.birth_instant),
    so the result is 6 October less the instant of attainment.

    Rounding to a thousandth of a month (under an hour) removes float error,
    so attaining the age exactly on 6 October, or exactly on 6 April six
    months earlier, counts as having attained it then.
    """
    age_in_months = grid_month(year, 10) - np.asarray(birth, dtype=np.float64)
    months_since = age_in_months - 12 * np.asarray(attained_age, dtype=np.float64)
    return np.round(months_since, 3)

import numpy as np

from policyengine_uk.model_api import *


class car_vehicle_excise_duty(Variable):
    value_type = float
    entity = Person
    definition_period = YEAR
    unit = GBP
    label = "Vehicle excise duty on this person's car"
    reference = "https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/22/schedule/1"

    def formula_2024(person, period, parameters):
        p = parameters(period).gov.dft.vehicle_excise_duty
        registration = person("car_first_registration_date", period)
        emissions = max_(person("car_co2_emissions", period), 0)
        engine = person("car_engine_size", period)
        price = person("car_list_price", period)
        fuel = person("car_fuel_type", period)
        fuel_types = fuel.possible_values
        zero_emission = fuel == fuel_types.ELECTRIC
        emissions = where(zero_emission, 0, emissions)
        alternative = fuel == fuel_types.ALTERNATIVE_FUEL

        # One twelve-month licence per VED rate year (1 April to 31 March),
        # with uninterrupted annual renewals since first registration.
        year_start = np.datetime64(f"{period.start.year}-04-01")
        year_end = np.datetime64(f"{period.start.year + 1}-04-01")
        registration_year = registration.astype("datetime64[Y]")
        registration_month = registration.astype("datetime64[M]")
        april = registration_year.astype("datetime64[M]") + np.timedelta64(3, "M")
        licence_year = (
            year_start.astype("datetime64[Y]").astype(int)
            - registration_year.astype(int)
            + (registration_month < april)
        )
        modern = registration >= np.datetime64(date(*p.modern_registration_start))
        graduated = registration >= np.datetime64(date(*p.graduated_registration_start))
        first_year_rate = where(
            fuel == fuel_types.DIESEL_NON_RDE2,
            p.first_year_diesel_non_rde2.calc(emissions, right=True),
            p.first_year.calc(emissions, right=True),
        )
        first_year_rate = max_(
            first_year_rate - alternative * p.alternative_fuel_discount, 0
        )
        threshold = where(
            zero_emission,
            p.zero_emission_expensive_car_threshold,
            p.expensive_car_threshold,
        )
        supplement = (
            (price > threshold)
            & (licence_year >= 1)
            & (licence_year <= p.supplement_years)
            & (
                ~zero_emission
                | (
                    registration
                    >= np.datetime64(
                        date(*p.zero_emission_supplement_registration_start)
                    )
                )
            )
        ) * p.expensive_car_supplement
        modern_rate = where(
            licence_year == 0,
            first_year_rate,
            p.standard_rate - alternative * p.alternative_fuel_discount + supplement,
        )
        graduated_emissions = where(
            registration < np.datetime64(date(*p.band_k_registration_cutoff)),
            min_(emissions, p.band_k_max_emissions),
            emissions,
        )
        graduated_rate = max_(
            p.graduated.calc(graduated_emissions, right=True)
            - alternative * p.alternative_fuel_discount,
            0,
        )
        engine_rate = where(
            (engine <= p.engine_size_threshold) | zero_emission,
            p.small_engine_rate,
            p.large_engine_rate,
        )
        charge = select(
            [modern, graduated], [modern_rate, graduated_rate], default=engine_rate
        )
        exempt = person("car_is_ved_exempt", period) | (
            zero_emission & p.zero_emission_exempt
        )
        return where((registration < year_end) & ~exempt, charge, 0)
